title: Density and Geometry Recovery from Nearest-Neighbor Graphs
statement: Let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be i.i.d. samples from a density $p$ on $\mathbb R^d$, and let $A$ be the adjacency matrix of their unweighted $k$-nearest-neighbor graph. Can $p(X_i)$ be estimated up to constant factors from $A$ alone, and can the sample locations be approximately reconstructed up to translation, rotation, and rescaling when $n$ is large?

## Literature review (checked 2026-08-21)

**Status:** partially solved

**Assessment.** The density can be estimated from an unweighted directed k-nearest-neighbor graph under the paper's sampling assumptions, and point localization has synchronization-based results, but general reconstruction up to the stated similarities is not fully solved.

**Sources checked.**

- [von Luxburg et al., density estimation from unweighted kNN graphs](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper/2013/hash/eae27d77ca20db309e056e3d2dcd7d69-Abstract.html)
- [point localization and density estimation from ordinal kNN graphs](https://arxiv.org/abs/1504.00722)
